summary.title: Software engineering practices
summary.one_liner: Seven practices that help development teams work better: keep docs in the code repo, generate test data, make schema migrations boring, use project templates, automate formatting, automate dev environment setup, and build automated preview environments.
takeaways: Keep documentation in the same repository as the code so reviews can require updates and docs are versioned with the code.
Build a synthetic test data system instead of importing production data, so engineers can reproduce edge cases safely.
Make schema changes routine by using version-controlled migrations and a multi-step process that keeps old and new code working during deploys.
Automate code formatting in CI with a fixed default configuration, and provide tested templates and one-command dev environment setup and PR preview environments.
summary.summary: Simon Willison expands on replies to a Twitter question about software engineering practices for development teams, rejecting the term "best practices" as prescriptive. He lists seven practices and explains each with reasoning and concrete examples, drawing on his experience with Django migrations, cookiecutter templates, and tools like Black, Gitpod, Codespaces, and hosting platforms that offer preview environments. The post is opinion-based experience rather than a formal tutorial.
